headline: South Asia: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?.
- Western Russia: Russia attacks substations connecting Kyiv to nuclear power plants and infrastructure overnight – Zelenskyy.
- India: Saudi strike kills 22 people, mostly women & kids, near Yemen's capital.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: SIMMER DOWN - Tougher sanctions needed to curb parliamentary tensions, lecturer warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 11 hours ago: SIMMER DOWN - Tougher sanctions needed to curb parliamentary tensions, lecturer warns.
With tensions in Jamaica’s Parliament escalating this week, a government lecturer is calling for tougher sanctions against lawmakers who breach parliamentary procedures, warning that failure to act could see the House of Representatives degenerate into a “brawl”.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 11 hours ago: Privy Council shuts door on Dawkins Brown’s fight to regain accountant’s licence.
The United Kingdom-based Judicial Committee of the Privy Council has refused Dawkins Brown permission to appeal his removal from Jamaica’s Register of Public Accountants, bringing his latest attempt to overturn the disciplinary decision to an end. The refusal, handed down last month, means Brown has failed to secure a hearing before Jamaica’s highest appellate court in his battle against the Public Accountancy Board (PAB), which struck him off the professional register in March 2020 and ordered him to pay $1.6 million towards the costs of its disciplinary proceedings.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 11 hours ago: Why achieving your goals can leave you feeling so empty.
THE CONVERSATION: When Anne Carson learned she had won the Nobel Prize in literature, she was in Iceland, where, according to the Swedish Academy, she was "listening to the wind". Carson didn't answer her phone right away, silencing it until her husband persuaded her to call back. Her verdict on the academy's choice: "I think you're all insane." Whatever she felt in the moment, there is an irony in Carson's Nobel win. The highest award in literature has gone to a writer who has spent her career exploring the emptiness of a desire fulfilled.
United States - bottom line: How Afghanistan War soul-searching led to renaming of Navy expeditionary command.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: How Afghanistan War soul-searching led to renaming of Navy expeditionary command.
The command's recent name change was years in the making after the end of the Afghanistan War, according to the head of Commander, Navy Expeditionary Forces.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russia attacks substations connecting Kyiv to nuclear power plants and infrastructure overnight – Zelenskyy.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Russia attacks substations connecting Kyiv to nuclear power plants and infrastructure overnight – Zelenskyy.
Russian forces launched a combined attack on Ukraine on the night of 6–7 November, using a total of 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles. All the missiles were launched towards Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast, targeting energy facilities and infrastructure.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Ukraine strikes factory in Russia’s Oryol with Neptune missiles – General Staff.
Ukrainian forces struck the Proton-Elektroteks military plant in Russia’s Oryol with Neptune missiles on 7 November, causing a fire and explosions at the facility.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Zelenskyy reports four Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's Pivnichnyi Bridge.
Ukrainian President Zelenskyy has stated that four Russian ballistic missiles struck the Pivnichnyi Bridge in Kyiv overnight on 6-7 November.
- Ukrainska Pravda, just now: Life in Kyiv becoming increasingly difficult – EU ambassador on Russian missile strike.
EU Ambassador to Ukraine Katarína Mathernová has commented on the latest Russian missile strike on Kyiv, highlighting the harsh reality of blackouts.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Serbian President’s Controversial Last-Minute Pardons Face Legal Challenges.
- Balkan Insight, one day ago: Serbian President’s Controversial Last-Minute Pardons Face Legal Challenges.
Before quitting as head of state, Aleksandar Vucic pardoned various suspects accused of violent attacks on anti-government protesters - decisions that critics say may be illegal and unconstitutional.
- Balkan Insight, one day ago: Transnistria’s Separatist Leader Decorated by Moscow, Denounced by Moldova.
Moldova has imposed a travel ban on breakaway Transnistria’s leader Vadim Krasnoselsky after Vladimir Putin gave him an award for upholding ‘Russian values’, sparking fresh controversy in the EU candidate state.

He stressed that any Iranian regime loyal to the Islamic Revolution "will always have the motivation to restore its capabilities," warning that this would include nuclear weapons if given the chance.

A region once offering refuge becomes increasingly dangerous, as 50 people are killed in a single attack.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Qeshm island and Hormuz hit, as mediators try to prevent US-Iran escalation.
US strikes have continued on Iran after more ships in the Strait of Hormuz were attacked.

Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency said earlier that initial reports indicated that two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, adding that there was no official information on possible damage.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 20 hours ago: South Africa: The Honeybadger's Revenge - Former Minister Dion George's Nuclear War Over SA's Captive Lions.

Africa - bottom line: Nigeria: Bandits Kill 2, Abduct 18 in Kaduna Community.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 22 hours ago: Nigeria: Bandits Kill 2, Abduct 18 in Kaduna Community.
[Daily Trust] Bandits have attacked Akwando village in Kuturmi, Kachia Local Government Area of Kaduna State, killing two persons and abducting 18 villagers.
- Africanews, one day ago: UN says struggling to help millions fleeing Sudan war find shelter.
The United Nations on Friday said about 15.4 million people who have fled conflict in Sudan need emergency shelter and essential household items, but humanitarian organisations are facing funding shortages.
- Africanews, 23 hours ago: Netherlands: Protesters storm Amsterdam data centre construction site.
Protesters broke into a data centre construction site intended for Microsoft in Amsterdam, on 6 November, climbing cranes and unfurling banners denouncing artificial intelligence and the company's alleged involvement in the war in Gaza.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, one day ago: Uganda: Police Warn Parents Against Online Radicalisation, Drug Abuse Among Children.
[Nile Post] Uganda Police have urged parents, guardians and community leaders to strengthen supervision of children during the school holidays, warning that increased exposure to the internet, peer pressure and limited parental guidance could expose them to drug abuse, radicalisation and criminal activities.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?.
A hysterical map on social media has cooked up an image of the blast radius of radioactive fallout if Iran’s nuclear facilities were attacked. It fancies that it shows how radiation would reach Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, parts of Afghanistan, and potentially other areas depending on atmospheric conditions.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Taipei Times, just now: Iran says forces ‘stronger’ than at beginning of war.
Iran said Saturday its military has grown “stronger” since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran’s nuclear programme. Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the Middle East conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February. Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: France braces for protests as Yellow Vests urge ‘mass disobedience’.
French unions and student groups are set to take to the streets for another day of protests on Saturday, while the Yellow Vests movement plans a separate rally in central Paris despite a ban by authorities. The demonstrations follow weeks of youth-led unrest and nationwide strikes that drew hundreds of thousands of workers protesting over the rising cost of living. They come less than six months before voters elect a new head of state to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in the opinion polls.
- The Hindu - International, 23 hours ago: Airstrikes on market in southwestern Yemen kill at least 30, Houthis say.
A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, told Houthi-run TV Al Masirah that 15 people were also wounded in the airstrikes on the market in al-Waziyah in the province of Taiz
India - bottom line: Saudi strike kills 22 people, mostly women & kids, near Yemen's capital.
- Times of India - Top Stories, The Hindu - International, 3 hours ago: Saudi strike kills 22 people, mostly women & kids, near Yemen's capital.
In a devastating escalation of conflict near Sanaa, Yemen, airstrikes have left 22 people dead and more than 30 wounded. This latest violence adds to the chaos following a previous assault at the al-Hadara market, where about 30 fatalities were reported. Houthi officials blame Saudi Arabia for the strikes, though Riyadh remains silent.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Iran distributes iodine pills near nuclear sites as Trump weighs fresh strikes.
Amid rising tensions and fears of US military action, Iran has reportedly begun issuing iodine tablets to individuals in proximity to its nuclear facilities. This proactive step is linked to discussions within the Trump administration regarding renewed military efforts to disrupt Iran's nuclear arsenal. Irag's leadership has expressed concerns about any strikes originating from their territory, signifying the complex geopolitical dynamics at play in the region.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Trump's makes nuclear push in space exploration, sets 2-yr deadline for Nasa's Mars mission.
NASA is gearing up to launch an innovative nuclear-powered spacecraft towards Mars within the next two years. This ambitious mission is set to pioneer advanced nuclear-electric propulsion technology, critical for future exploration efforts. With a focus on returning astronauts to the Moon, the subsequent establishment of a human presence on Mars signifies America’s commitment to ambitious space ventures, aiming to harness the potential of nuclear propulsion for deep space travel.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Goalkeeper considers retirement after collision that led to Tenerife striker's death.
Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono is reportedly considering retiring from professional football after being left deeply traumatised by the death of Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel following an on-field collision on November 2. The 30-year-old forward died in hospital the next morning. Owono is receiving psychological support from his club as he struggles to process the tragedy, according to Mundo Deportivo.

- South China Morning Post - China, 12 hours ago: Trump confirms fresh Iran strikes days after voters punish war at polls.
US President Donald Trump said the American military on Friday carried out new limited strikes on Iran, targeting an Iranian air defence system. Iranian state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, which is in a crucial waterway for oil shipments. Trump in an exchange with reporters described the military action as “minor”. “They knocked out – they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five,” he told...

A Guatemalan ⁠lawmaker and three ⁠police officers were ⁠killed in an armed attack in the eastern department of Zacapa, President Bernardo Arevalo said, condemning the violence and ordering security forces to ‌help identify those responsible. Lawmaker Julio Cesar Portillo Paz was attacked on Friday in Rio Hondo, Zacapa, and initially taken to a hospital with serious injuries. His death was later confirmed by the ⁠National Unity of Hope party, or UNE, to which he ‌belonged. Arevalo said the three...

Washington is offering a US$20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear programme, the US military has said, as President Donald Trump reiterated that Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war. A State Department programme, Rewards for Justice, “is offering a reward of up to US$20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear programme, including its facilities, equipment and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific...

Myanmar’s military-backed government may find its reluctance to address the international community’s concerns a greater obstacle to economic recovery than the threat of tougher international financial restrictions, according to analysts. Australia - bottom line: Who Gives A Crap confirms customer data exposed in third party software breach.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: Who Gives A Crap confirms customer data exposed in third party software breach.
Hackers accessed names, contact details and total spend, but not payment details or passwords, the company said.
- The Guardian - Australia, 3 hours ago: They have gone 10 weeks without answers. Will these families ever know what happened to loved ones missing after Nepal’s floods?.
From Sydney to South Africa, they text loved ones with no reply and respond to questions they can’t answer. But some still hold hope Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Every day, Nikhila Agastya answers more questions from her two children: has she heard anything about their father? Is he with anyone? Is it snowing in Kathmandu? Is he cold, and does he have warm clothing? Will he come home? The answer is: probably not. “They know that [their] father is missing,” Nikhila says. “And they are still looking for him. They always wait; every day they wait for him.
- ABC News Australia, 14 hours ago: Elders call for leadership to address Indigenous child safety crisis.
Indigenous elders accuse WA Aboriginal Affairs Minister Don Punch of "passing the buck" on child protection in the state's north, and say they want leaders who will listen and offer a clear plan forward.
- The Guardian - Australia, 16 hours ago: Ben Roberts-Smith collaborates with gym business run by influencer that sold ‘war crimes’ pre-workout supplement.
Zero Limits supplements is co-owned by rightwing podcaster and fitness coach Chris Katelaris, also known as ‘Big Chocky’ Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Ben Roberts-Smith has collaborated with a gym supplements company run by a rightwing influencer which recently sold a pre-workout product called “war crimes”.
